transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-08
Time: 15:30 PT / 23:30 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (SE), Priya (CSM), Lena (Cumulus Head of AI), Tom (Platform Lead), Rita (FinOps), Samir (CTO joined at 00:10)

Auto-summary (brief): discussed three traffic scenarios, agreed to benchmark, security docs to be shared, follow-up scheduled.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. we wanted to run through adoption velocity and map out capacity scenarios for the upcoming search-personalization launch. is that still the right framing?
[00:08] Lena: yeah that's perfect. we're projecting a pretty quick ramp — could be 5x baseline in the first week if the A/B goes wide.
[00:14] Tom: and, yeah, the platform team wants to understand if we need to pre-commit or rely on burst/dedicated during the first 10 days.
[00:22] Diego: okay, so we usually model three scenarios — steady-state, growth (gradual ramp), and spike (launch). we'll also show the unit cost delta between hosted instances vs dedicated reserved pools.
[00:30] Rita: quick Q — how do you calculate tokens for embeddings vs generation? our FinOps show embeddings are a huge driver.
[00:36] Maya: great point. we'll split tokens by generation and embeddings in the spreadsheet, and include per-embedding vector cost and batch-level discounts.
[00:44] Tom: another constraint: our data residency rules require logs to remain in regional storage, and for private PII flows we want VPC. how much extra ops overhead is Private vs Redwood Hosted?
[00:53] Priya: in our experience with similar accounts, Private has more initial setup and a small steady monthly platform fee, but gives you control for audit and KMS integrations. hosted + dedicated burst is often the sweet spot for quick launches.
[01:05] Lena: Samir, do you have anything to add on compliance?
[01:08] Samir: sorry for joining late — yes, SOC2 is table stakes, and we need a KMS/HSM path. if Private requires too much lead time we'll need a fallback plan.
[01:14] Diego: noted. For capacity numbers, can you share expected QPS windows and token sizes? we can estimate KV cache hit rates — by the way i might say KV cash in the doc later, lol, the transcript does that often.
[01:24] Tom: mmh, example: baseline 200 QPS, average prompt 120 tokens, embeddings 15 per second during indexing. peak could be 1k QPS during launch days.
[01:34] Rita: and on cost governance, we want alerts at 50% and 80% of weekly spend forecast, with a hard stop if we exceed commit by 20%.
[01:42] Maya: good, we'll model alert bands. we'll also show p50/p95 latency impacts when enabling prefix caching and different batching profiles.
[01:50] Lena: can you show an example where we trade latency for cost? e.g., higher batching to reduce tokens but p95 goes up?
[01:58] Diego: yep, that's the classic tradeoff. we'll include multiple kernel/quantization profiles that Redwood Optimize would recommend per workload.
[02:06] Tom: for the benchmark, can you run our sample prompts and a synthetic spike test? we want to validate cold-starts and KV cache warm ups.
[02:14] Diego: absolutely — we'll run a 2-hour synthetic spike and a 6-hour steady run. need to coordinate timing because GPUs for dedicated pools are scheduled.
[02:22] Rita: what about the procurement timeline for reserved capacity? if we need guaranteed throughput for launch, how fast can Dedicated be provisioned?
[02:30] Priya: provisioning depends on the region and capacity availability; in many cases we can provision burst pools in 48–72 hours if there's headroom. full Reserved contracts take longer (billing/legal).
[02:40] Lena: we're leaning towards hosted with dedicated burst for launch and then evaluate Private if adoption persists. do we have real numbers for the delta in unit cost?
[02:48] Maya: we'll provide per-token cost comparisons across the three scenarios and show break-even points for a monthly commit.
[02:54] Tom: also, can you include a sensitivity analysis for embedding index growth? our index will grow quickly and embeddings cost could dominate.
[03:02] Diego: yes, we'll model embedding growth and cache hit-rate assumptions. note that caching embeddings is different than prefix caching for generation. sometimes the model will pull vectors from an index that lives outside the inference path.
[03:14] Rita: small thing — how do you handle audit logs retention for Private vs Hosted? our compliance needs 2 year retention with immutable logs.
[03:22] Priya: Private can route logs to your SIEM and meet retention. Hosted has configurable retention tiers — we'll add a compliance column in the spreadsheet.
[03:32] Lena: risk: if we under-provision, we'll see latency spikes and user friction. over-provisioning costs money. need to find middle ground.
[03:38] Maya: agreed. that's why the scenario planning exercise is helpful — you can pick a commit size for a 90-day runway and use alerts to protect budget during spikes.
[03:46] Samir: are there recommended guardrails for rollout—maybe canary percentages tied to cost burn?
[03:52] Diego: yes, rollouts can be throttled by route and model variant. you can enforce route-level quotas and automatic fallback to a cheaper model if cost thresholds hit. we'll show a sample rollout plan.
[04:02] Tom: on telemetry — can we get token-level breakdowns per route? we want to attribute spend to product teams.
[04:08] Maya: Redwood Console supports token-level tagging and per-route dashboards. we'll include screenshots in the follow-up pack.
[04:16] Lena: any blockers on our side?
[04:18] Tom: need to anonymize sample prompts and confirm the PST test window (we are global).
[04:22] Rita: i'll confirm FinOps thresholds and procurement lead times.
[04:26] Maya: great. recap — we'll send the cost spreadsheet, security doc links, and benchmark plan. Diego will coordinate the benchmark run with Tom. meet again 2027-02-22 to finalize pilot kickoff.
[04:36] Priya: i'll also include a short playbook for emergency scale-up in case the launch exceeds forecasts.
[04:40] Lena: thanks all — this was helpful.
[04:42] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in Slack and send the doc pack by EOD tomorrow.
[04:46] Tom: thanks, bye.

(occasional overlaps and small transcription errors: "KV cash" appears where KV cache likely meant; speaker labels sometimes simplified; timestamps approximate)
